clue.text: Bacon, perhaps, with bitter lacking head at first

indicators.note: a word lacking its head has lost its opening letter, so the synonym for bitter is cut at the front

parts.note: bitter, sharp-tasting, means tart
first is written 1st, and the 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone is drinking a pint of flat beer alongside a breakfast of bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking head' takes the T off TART to leave ART; 'at' just places the next piece beside it. Francis Bacon was a twentieth-century painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was a painter, so he is an example of a person who makes art.

clue.text: Boy, male, then female?

definitions.note: a noun: the word female is an instance of the opposite term to male

parts.note: Antony is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A list of family members runs boy, man, then a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: After ANTONY and M, 'then' leads to the definition: female is the word of opposite meaning to male, which the clue just mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Female is the word of opposite meaning to male, so it is an example of this kind of word.

clue.text: Accepting point, bite tongue through the nose?

indicators.note: one piece accepting another takes it inside, so the word for bite holds the point

parts.note: bite, a sharp flavour, means tang
W, west, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone takes a sharp remark and bites their tongue, snorting through the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' here means language or way of speaking, not the body part, so a tongue through the nose is nasal speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal quality of speech, a way of talking that seems to come through the nose.

clue.text: I'm blessed with Posh and Spinal Tap endlessly rocking

indicators.note: rocking suggests something shaken about, so the combined letters are jumbled

parts.note: U means upper-class, so posh, in British slang

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the band's name

explanation.surface: A fan is thrilled that Posh Spice has joined the band Spinal Tap on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Spinal Tap less its last letter gives SPINALTA; add U and rearrange. Posh is also Victoria Beckham of the Spice Girls, a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A saint is a holy person, so a saint speaking could say of themself that they are blessed.

clue.text: Heavy ball

definitions.meaning: a heavy is a burly man hired for muscle, such as a doorman at a club
in cricket, a short-pitched delivery that rears up at the batsman

explanation.definitionFit: A bouncer is both a doorman employed as muscle and a cricket delivery that rises sharply.

clue.text: Needing no introduction, moorland follows mountain to its relative position?

indicators.note: follows puts the moorland piece after the mountain piece

parts.note: Ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: a word needing no introduction loses its first letter, so the moorland word is cut at the front

parts.note: a heath is an area of open moorland

explanation.surface: A guidebook explains how a stretch of moorland sits in relation to a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needing no introduction' removes the opening letter, and 'follows' puts that piece second. The definition is a riddle: where does moorland lie relative to a mountain?
explanation.definitionFit: Moorland at the foot of a mountain lies under it, so its relative position is below.

clue.text: Ahead in the tennis match, but not happy

parts.note: up means ahead in a contest, as in a goal up
a set is one of the units a tennis match is divided into

explanation.surface: A tennis player is leading the match but still looks miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upset means being distressed, the reverse of being happy.

clue.text: No time for devious, egocentric caretaker

indicators.note: devious means taking a winding route, so the remaining letters are reordered
no time for removes the letter standing for time from the word that follows

explanation.surface: A building's caretaker has no patience with a sly, self-centred tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: Take T from EGOCENTRIC to leave EGOCENRIC, which 'devious' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A concierge looks after a block of flats or a hotel entrance, which is a caretaker's role.

clue.text: Head of State during rule to abdicate

indicators.note: during means the letter goes within the word for rule

parts.note: to reign is to rule as monarch

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word State

explanation.surface: A head of state is told to give up the throne while still in power.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne or office, which is to resign it.

clue.text: Fuel runs out, first half lost?

annotationWithheld.why: Fuel runs out, first half lost? (6): DIESEL; runs out gives DIES, but no reading of 'first half lost' gives EL, and no source found for the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Fuel runs out, first half lost?

clue.text: Usual practice of one missile turning into dud

indicators.note: turning means the pair of pieces for one missile is read backwards

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
a dart is a small thrown missile

indicators.note: dud means faulty, so the letters of the word into are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: It is customary for a single missile to turn out to be a dud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses IDART to TRADI; 'dud' rearranges INTO as TION.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a custom handed down, a usual practice of a group.

clue.text: Space for a quarter in the Guardian

parts.note: S, south, is a quarter of the compass
a newspaper writing about itself says us, so the Guardian is us

explanation.surface: A newspaper is offering space for a coin worth a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appeared in the Guardian, so 'the Guardian' means we or US, as the paper would say of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is a hollow space in the bone of the skull, a cavity.

clue.text: See 22
Remarkable bird, end of parrot caged

indicators.note: caged means the letter is shut inside the bird's name

parts.note: a starling is a common bird

indicators.note: end of selects the final letter of the word parrot

explanation.surface: A remarkable bird has the tip of a parrot trapped inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means surprising, so something remarkable could be called startling.

clue.text: Right man who had miracle transformation?

definitions.note: a man of the political right, a Conservative politician

indicators.note: transformation means the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A man of good fortune was apparently transformed by a miracle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the right: Michael Howard led the Conservative Party, though the surface suggests a righteous man.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Howard was a Conservative Home Secretary and party leader, a politician of the right.

clue.text: I'm dirty when working, or I'm clean when working

definitions.note: a speaker who gets grimy on the job

indicators.note: working is a common signal of letters put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A worker says they get filthy on the job and clean only when off it.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'when working' is the trick: first in the definition, then as the anagram signal for OR I'M CLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal miner is blackened with coal dust on every shift, so dirty when working.

clue.text: See 13
Hawk and wren go off to collect wing

indicators.note: to collect means the rearranged letters gather another piece inside them
off means gone wrong, so the letters of wren go are jumbled

parts.note: an arm is a wing of an organisation, as in the armed forces

explanation.surface: A hawk and a small bird take off, sweeping up a wing together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges WRENGO into WONGER, which holds ARM. Hawk here is a political hawk, someone pushing for war.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawk is someone who argues for military action, so a warmonger.

clue.text: Might this be a deterrent for tease about to use tongue endlessly?

indicators.note: about means the word for tease is turned round

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the word for using the tongue

parts.note: to lick is to use the tongue

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether licking a person to tease them would put them off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RAG into GAR; 'endlessly' cuts LICK to LIC. The deterrent is for vampires, by legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore garlic wards off vampires, so it serves as a deterrent.

clue.text: City was smart once

parts.note: chic means stylish, smart
ago means in the past, once

explanation.surface: A place was fashionable at one time.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a large city in Illinois in the United States.

clue.text: Spy novelist

definitions.meaning: Guy ..., one of the Cambridge spies who passed secrets to the Soviets
Anthony ..., author of A Clockwork Orange

explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to both Guy, the Soviet spy, and Anthony, the novelist.

clue.text: Capital understood to be snatched by "Crusher"

indicators.note: to be snatched by means one piece is grabbed and held inside the other

parts.note: a boa is a snake that kills by crushing
got means understood, as in I got it

explanation.surface: A capital city is said to have been seized by a man known as Crusher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crusher' looks like a gangster's nickname; it is the snake, a boa constrictor.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogota is the capital city of Colombia.

clue.text: In mother and father you should be able to, as boils

parts.note: you should be able to see, the verb left unsaid
each of the words mother and father contains the letters of the word the, so both hold the's

explanation.surface: Parents are said to be visibly furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'in mother and father you should be able to see the's', each word holding THE; 'as' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that seethes bubbles or boils, and a person seethes with anger.

clue.text: Safety is simple: no drug for smoker

indicators.note: no means the drug letter is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: simple means easy
E stands for ecstasy, a drug
a lum is a chimney in Scots, something that smokes

explanation.surface: A smoker is told safety is simple: just stop taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: EASY without E gives ASY. LUM is a Scottish word for a chimney, hence 'smoker'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or refuge given to someone, so a place of safety.

clue.text: Badger 13, 15?

definitions.meaning: a creature that comes out after dark, a nocturnal animal
Ann Widdecombe said there was this quality about the politician at 13 and 15

explanation.walkthrough: Ann Widdecombe, a fellow Conservative, said of her former boss that he had this sinister air about him.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase suits a nocturnal badger and was a famous gibe at a Conservative leader.

clue.text: Point at heart of electrics, instrument blown

indicators.note: at heart of picks the central letter of the word electrics

parts.note: a horn is a musical instrument played by blowing

explanation.surface: An electrician finds a fault at the centre of the wiring and a horn blown.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on a plant stem, which is a point.

clue.text: See 22
One's proposed to a good man

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A woman is proposed to by a decent man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proposed' suggests marriage, but a toast is proposed at a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast is something proposed, as a drink in someone's honour.

clue.text: Fast for leader of orchestra, or not

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of the word orchestra

explanation.surface: An orchestra's leader wonders whether to play fast or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or not' means not fast, so slow, the musical term the answer gives; 'Fast' is the period of Lent, not speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the musical direction for slowly, the opposite of fast.

clue.text: Sign of month about to hit hard

indicators.note: about means the month abbreviation is placed around the next word

parts.note: Aug is short for August, a month
to rap is to hit sharply
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A sign of the month is about to hit hard.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is a person's signature, something they sign.

clue.text: Horse, Napoleon's initial ride, his horse?

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: initial picks the first letter of the name Napoleon

parts.note: a go is a turn, as a ride on a fairground horse

explanation.surface: A rider asks about Napoleon's first mount and whether it was his horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers back to Napoleon: Marengo was his famous grey charger.
explanation.definitionFit: Marengo was the name of Napoleon's favourite war horse, named after one of his battles.

clue.text: Soldiers accepting deserter should be free

indicators.note: accepting means the soldiers take the deserter inside

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is someone who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: Troops who take in a runaway soldier should let him go free.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means without charge, free of cost.
